BH-1938. The lane's kill switch: 0 stops the backup before anything runs (flags/state-backup-off is the other). bin/state-backup.sh has no literal for it and tests it as ${STATE_BACKUP:-} = 0: row > cached row > env > this default. bin/lib/backup-freshness.sh still reads only env/global.env and the flag when it decides a box is deliberately off, so a row 0 shows that box as stale there.

BH-6173. zstd level for the archive, run as `zstd -<level> -T1`. Required: bin/state-backup.sh has no literal for it and reads ${BACKUP_ZSTD_LEVEL:-} (row > cached row > env > this default; empty only in a scratch tree, where 1 answers). A value outside 1-19 is logged and 1 is used. Level 1 measured 34% less CPU than 3 for a 16% bigger object.

BH-6173. 1: a run whose input manifest matches the last shipped object ships nothing (after a head-object of that object) and only moves .ts in state/backup-last.json. 0: every run ships. Required: bin/state-backup.sh has no literal for it and reads ${BACKUP_SKIP_UNCHANGED:-}; a value other than 0 or 1 is logged and 1 is used.

BH-6173. A full upload at least once per this many hours even when no input changed. Required: bin/state-backup.sh has no literal for it and reads ${BACKUP_FORCE_HOURS:-}; a value that is not a positive number is logged and 24 is used.

BH-6173. 1 ships even when no input changed. Read by bin/state-backup.sh as ${BACKUP_FORCE:-} (empty or 0 = not forced). NOT settable from the control plane: it is the operator and test seam, set by bin/box-ops.sh backup_now so "back up now" always uploads.
